about: Zone-of-render fixtures, Option D (ruled 2026-09-24). Self-authored; expected zones written 2026-09-25 before any synthesis call. Records are in the SYNTHESIS INPUT shape and go to synthesize() as one morning. Flight numbers and codes are fake. Only membership, render_zone and end_render_zone are asserted; container and primary are not. Cases f1 and f2 (r24's twin and its non-home twin) added 2026-09-27 for fix shape (B), expected zones written from airports.py before any call.

records.summary: Flight: AA 9001 from TPA to DFW
Flight AA 9001 from Tampa (TPA) to Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW)
Hotel check-in at Fixture Suites Downtown Chicago

expected.why: Twin of the 2026-09-18 AA flight group (r6/r7/r14/r19). r1 is the parser twin: stored New York at both ends, arrival 17:13 NY, the wrong zone for a DFW landing. The records name TPA/Tampa and DFW/Dallas/Fort Worth, so the text gives Tampa at the start and Dallas at the end. end_zone is withheld from the model, so Chicago must come from the text, not from r2's stored end.

Gmail only, stored zone null, airport codes and no city names: ATL is Atlanta (Eastern), DEN is Denver (Mountain). Checks that the model infers from codes. Since 2026-09-27 codes_only matches r5, so both zones come from airports.py (fix shape (B)); this case now checks the override, not the model's inference.
Hotel naming a city (Chicago), no airport code, no confirmation code. The group ends where it starts, so end_render_zone equals render_zone (Finding 7 ruling, 2026-09-25).
Portland alone: Oregon (America/Los_Angeles) or Maine (America/New_York). Nothing else in the record picks one, so the place is ambiguous and both keys are null.

Names no place. Deliberately a calendar record carrying a stored America/New_York zone: the stored zone is not text naming a place, so the model must write null rather than copy it. The null falls back to the stored zone at render, so the page is the same either way; this checks the rule, not the page.

Added 2026-09-27, written before any call: the live twin of 09-11 r24 (gmail appointment, 'Departing flight TPA to DFW', empty location, null zones, a flight number and a confirmation code). r24's start zone drew New York or null from the model on an unchanged request. codes_only matches it, so both zones come from airports.py (TPA, DFW) and are deterministic by construction. Its own date, so rule 2 cannot merge it into case (a).

Added 2026-09-27, written before any call: f1's shape with a non-home origin (LAX). TPA is HOME_TZ, so r24's null was page-invariant; a null or wrong start here would show on the page once path (a) renders it. Both zones from airports.py (LAX, DFW); this is the fixture that proves the override, not the prompt.
